name: Flash UI: AI Swarm Vibecoding Studio
tag: Describe the screen you need and a team of agents plans, designs and builds working components.

scenarios.title: Build a booking widget
scenarios.ask: Build a booking widget for a dental office: pick a service, date and time. {variants} design options, {style} style.
steps: Planner
Split the request into 3 parts: service list, calendar and time slots, plus a confirm screen.
Designer agents
Produced {variants} layouts in a {style} style, all using the same spacing and color tokens.
Builder agents
Wrote working components for each layout with keyboard support and empty states.
Tester
Clicked through each option and checked contrast. Fixed {variants} small issues.
Exporter
Packaged the chosen option as React components with a preview link.
followups: Can I edit the result by talking to it?
Yes. Say what to change, like making the time slots bigger, and only the affected component is rebuilt.
Does it work with our design system?
Load your tokens and component list and the designer agents use them instead of their defaults.

scenarios.title: Turn a spreadsheet into an admin screen
scenarios.ask: Make an admin table for our {rows} inventory items with {cols} columns, search, filters and inline edit.
steps: Planner
Read the column names and guessed types: text, number, date and status.
Designer agent
Laid out a table with sticky headers, {=min(cols, 4)} filter chips and a search box.
Builder agents
Built sorting, paging at 50 rows and inline edit with undo.
Tester
Loaded {rows} sample rows and checked that sorting and filters stay fast.
followups: Is it connected to our database?
Not yet. It ships with a data adapter you point at your API. Until then it runs on the sample rows.
Can it handle much more data?
For tens of thousands of rows, ask for server-side paging and the builder agents switch the table to fetch pages on demand.

scenarios.title: Redesign a sign-up flow
scenarios.ask: Our sign-up flow has {screens} screens and {drop}% of people drop off. Redesign it.
steps: Reviewer
Walked the {screens} screens and listed {=screens * 2} fields, {=max(1, screens - 2)} of them optional.
Planner
Proposed {=max(2, ceil(screens / 2))} screens by moving optional fields after sign-up.
Designer agents
Drew the new flow with a progress bar and clear error messages.
Builder agents
Built it as working components with form validation.

result.title: New flow
rows: A/B test against the current flow

followups: Shorter flows often help, but it is not guaranteed. Run an A/B test and the studio can build both versions with tracking events.
What happens to the optional fields?
They move to a profile step after sign-up, where people can fill them in later.
